findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/rail_reading.rs:510-515 (the comment above labelCentreAnswered and labelLiesOver) and crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_ui_nav_polish.rs:16-20 plus the comment above then_the_revealed_word_can_be_read
findings.obligation: A reading states what it can see, and the words of the oracle claim no observation the oracle does not make. Risk Y10 names two distinct causes - an ancestor that clips the revealed word, and page content painted over it - so a claim to tell them apart is a claim about evidence.
findings.observation: Both comments say that naming the element which answered the hit test is what tells those two causes apart in a failure. It cannot tell them apart. A clipped word is not painted, so the point answers the lane or the card under it; a covered word is painted below that same lane or card, so the point answers the same node. My run shows it: with the shipped stylesheet holding BOTH causes at once, labelCentreAnswered reads article.issue-card GEN-5 for Invite a member and article.issue-card GEN-2 for Keyboard shortcuts, which names the covering work and not the cause. The falsifier is sound and stays sound - the row is red while either cause holds, and green only when neither does - so only the diagnostic claim is overstated.
findings.remediation: Either reword the two comments to say what the field really gives - the thing the operator sees instead of her word, which does not separate a clip from a cover - or add one reading that does separate them, for example whether any ancestor between the word and the rail declares a scroll port or a clip. Do not change the assertion: it already refuses both causes.

findings.obligation: ADR-NAV-POLISH-002 and law L7: a rail control the operator finds by its own visible word owes its word 4.5 to 1 instead of a 3 to 1 boundary, and a control inside .app-shell with no visible word keeps the boundary rule.
findings.observation: This is the round-one finding, carried forward because nothing in this delta resolves it. ADR-NAV-POLISH-002 is unchanged since 79da33d, and ADR-NAV-POLISH-003, -004 and -005 do not touch the exemption. The reworded row now makes the key explicit - the visible word - and the probe reads a word only where it is drawn, since wordOf skips a node with a clip-path. In the narrowed geometry and at phone width the two lower controls draw no word, so they fall on the wordless side and owe the 3 to 1 boundary the quiet lower group removes. The scenario opens the open desk geometry alone, so neither the scope of the law nor the shipped result is observed in those two geometries. Non-blocking for craft, exactly as in round one.
findings.remediation: Decide in ADR-NAV-POLISH-002 whether the exemption belongs to the rail-control class in every geometry, as exactly as the rail links are suggests, or only where a word is actually drawn. If only where a word is drawn, say what identifies the two narrowed controls instead. The oracle then adds the row for the decided geometry.

MEASURED RED of the two new word rows, my own run, not the author report. argv: scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=ui-nav-polish timeout --kill-after=60 2400 cargo test -p foundry-acceptance", exit 101. Summary: 30 scenarios, 28 passed, 2 failed; 194 steps, 192 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are the outline The word the narrowed nav reveals can be read over her board, at feature_ui_nav_polish.rs:676. Invite a member: labelPresent true, labelInTheLayout true, labelBox 114.5 by 26.9 px, labelCentreIsBesideTheRail true, labelLiesOver section.column and article.issue-card GEN-5, labelCentreHitsTheLabel FALSE, labelCentreAnswered article.issue-card GEN-5. Keyboard shortcuts: the same, over three pieces of page content, labelCentreAnswered article.issue-card GEN-2. The two guards that come first - a word is shown at all, and the word is drawn beside the strip over board content - both PASSED, so the red is the law itself and not a setup failure. That is semantic RED for the declared reason, with production at HEAD keeping overflow-y auto on the folded rail and no z-index on .sidebar.

THE ROW CAN GO GREEN ONLY WHEN THE WORD IS TRULY PAINTED ON TOP, read against the shipped stylesheet at crates/foundry-app/static/css/foundry.b3a70ff6.css. .sidebar is position sticky, top 0, height 100vh, overflow-y auto, with NO z-index; [data-nav-collapsed] .sidebar adds no overflow override; the folded label is position absolute at left 100 percent plus 8 px, clipped to a 1 px box and revealed on focus-visible at z-index 30; .column and .issue-card are position relative at z-index auto and come later in the document. Two independent causes therefore hold the row red. Fix the clip alone and the word still paints under the column, so the hit test still answers the column. Fix the paint level alone and the folded scroll container still clips the word out of view, so it is not painted at all. Both fixes together, and only then, make the word the thing painted at its own centre. A fourth wrong implementation is also refused: moving the word back inside the strip fails the second guard, because labelCentreIsBesideTheRail goes false and labelLiesOver goes empty.

The two bounding rows pass today and stay the guard against the two over-corrections the band forbids: a rail lifted above the overlays, and a flyout drawn in the open geometry.

THE THREE CORRECTIONS OF ROUND ONE, read in the bytes. F2, the glyph-only count in assert_shape_identifies_wordless_controls: the counter now increments only when glyph is true AND the word is empty after trimming, which is the remediation asked for. The probe reads a word through wordOf, which skips any node that is clipped, display none, visibility hidden or opacity zero, so a worded control cannot satisfy the count. F3, the row wording: the feature row and its step regex both now read a nav control the operator finds by its own visible word, which is what the reading actually turns on, and no orphan of the old sentence is left anywhere under crates. F4, the ink alpha: parse_colour keeps the alpha it parsed, blend_over paints the declared ink over the opaque surface behind it, and the 4.5 to 1 comparison now reads the blended ink, so a word painted at alpha zero is refused by the legibility reading instead of passing as solid ink. All three corrections are what their findings asked for.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED. The delta-2 oracle is public, independent, complete over law L8 and red for the declared reason. Law L8 closes case by case: a primary nav member and a lower-group member in the folded geometry over a long board page, the overlay that must cover the rail, and the open geometry where no word is revealed. The two word rows are measured RED at my own run - ui-nav-polish 30 scenarios, 28 passed, 2 failed, both at the hit test, with an issue card answering the centre of the revealed word while the two guards before it passed - and they can go green only when the folded strip stops clipping the word AND the rail takes a paint level above the positioned board content, because either cause alone keeps the point answering the lane.
